text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Canary pool 'runtime-serve-canary' memory surge and elevated 5xx rate (since 2178004280). Auto-rollback attempted but stalled during traffic drain. Paging SRE oncall. Link: https://console.redwood/infr/alerts/2178004280

Sam W: oncall here, what's the impact? any customer-facing errors?

Devon K: we're seeing a steady increase in OOMs on canary replicas after the new rollout. Error pattern: java.lang.OutOfMemoryError on seq-processing worker. Canary traffic is ~5% of prod and it's spiking 5xxs to several customers (observability shows request rate same, latency up).

Priya S: automated rollback started at 2178004400 via rollout policy, but drain stalled: some connections in pool won't close and envoy keeps routing 20% traffic. Logs show stuck upstream connections:
```
[2026-06-12T03:46:02Z] upstream reset: connection lingered, pid=4521, sock_state=CLOSE_WAIT
[2026-06-12T03:46:07Z] drain attempt 4/5: waiting for in-flight classes: seq-processing
```

Maria L: can we flip the feature flag for the new seq-path? If we cut the new path at the flag level, it should stop the memory-heavy code from executing immediately. Flag name: ff/seq-processing-v2.

Devon K: yes we can flip it. But note: config service has a small lag; safe sequence: 1) set flag=false (tiered rollout off), 2) verify no new heavy allocations in canary logs, 3) continue traffic drain.

Sam W: Maria, please do the flag flip and call out when done. Also notify Customer Success.

Maria L: flipping now -> `redwood feature-flag set ff/seq-processing-v2 false --env canary` -> done. API returned 200.

deploy-bot: Automated rollback job still shows drain=stalled. rollback_job_id=rb-20260612-01 status=stalled.

Devon K: logs after flag flip show immediate drop in mem allocs in new stack, but some pods still at high RSS (likely GC not yet reclaimed). Sending a soft restart to the canary replicas to accelerate reclaim. Command: `kc -n runtime set env deploy/canary-replica FORCE_GC=1 && kc -n runtime rollout restart deploy/canary-replica`

SRE Pager: hold on with restarts until traffic is removed from particular pods. We don't want to kill in-flight requests. Steps I'm executing: 1) mark pods as drain in service registry 2) wait 30s 3) cordon pod -> remove from LB -> then restart. I'll run the commands and post output.

SRE Pager: `kubectl annotate pod runtime-canary-abcde redwood/draining=true` -> annotated.

SRE Pager: `kubectl delete pod runtime-canary-abcde --grace-period=120` -> deletion started, graceful termination window set. kube-proxy and envoy will stop sending new requests.

Devon K: see logs: the pod termination triggered GC and RSS dropped from 2.4G -> 560M in ~40s. Good.

SRE Pager: doing this for the remaining 3 canary pods. Progress: 2/4 drained and restarted, one more draining, last one in CLOSE_WAIT still.

Sam W: Customer Success - Evan, can you ping the top 3 customers on canary who reported errors and let them know we're mitigating, may see brief retry spikes?

Customer Success - Evan: pinged customers A, B, C. A said they saw 500s in webhooks; B saw queued retries but no data loss; C hasn't replied yet. I'll escalate to C if they don't ack in 10m.

deploy-bot: rollback job rb-20260612-01 now shows drain progress 70% -> traffic shifted to stable.

Priya S: quick sanity checks to verify rollback health: 1) run smoke through canary path -> expect 200s 2) check token consumption still within baseline 3) check latency p95 back to normal. I'll run them now.

Priya S: smoke test -> all endpoints that hit seq-processing now returning 200 in canary after flag flip and pod restarts. p95 latency at 180ms (baseline 160ms) temporary bump acceptable.

Sam W: any database connection issues while draining? we had a previous incident with lingering DB sessions.

Devon K: DB sessions tied to the old seq-path are being closed as pods terminate. No abnormal locks observed. Running `select count(*) from pg_stat_activity where state <> 'idle'` -> counts are normal.

SRE Pager: rollback job completed: rb-20260612-01 status=complete at 2178005720. Canary traffic now <= 0.5%. Monitoring: 5xx rate back to baseline.

Maria L: flipping ff/seq-processing-v2 back to true on stable? No, keep false until postmortem and patch. We'll roll forward with a fix in the code path and a new canary once validated.

Sam W: handoff: I'll leave notes for the night oncall. Key items: - Cause: memory spike in seq-processing v2 under canary load - Mitigation: feature flag disable + controlled pod drain + targeted restarts - Risk: brief retry spikes and webhook 500s for small subset of customers - Next: PR with GC-region fix and better connection shutdowns; plan new canary only after synthetic pass.

Sam W: tagging owners: @Devon K (runtime fix), @Maria L (flag gating + rollout policy), @Priya S (verification harness), @Customer Success - Evan (customer comms).

Customer Success - Evan: customers A and B acknowledged, C still pending. I'll follow up.

Sam W: closing active page and marking incident as mitigated. We'll run a postmortem tomorrow morning 1000 in #postmortems. Please add logs, span ids, and the rollback job id to the meeting thread.

Devon K: saving kernel/core heap profiles, adding to the meeting notes.

incident-bot: Incident marked as resolved at 2178005829. Severity downgraded to SEV2 for follow-up work.

Sam W: thanks all. :thumbsup:
